purpose: Gentamicin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the blood, lungs, skin, urinary tract, and abdomen. It is also used in eye drop or ointment form to treat bacterial eye infections. Doctors usually prescribe it when other antibiotics are not strong enough to fight the infection.
how_it_works: Gentamicin works by stopping harmful bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive and grow. Without these proteins, the bacteria cannot function properly and eventually die. This helps your body clear the infection more quickly.
common_side_effects: When given by injection or IV, you may experience nausea, vomiting, headache, or dizziness. Some people notice redness, stinging, or mild irritation when using the eye drops or ointment. Let your doctor know if any side effects bother you.
warnings: Gentamicin can sometimes harm your kidneys or affect your hearing and balance, especially if used for a long time or at high doses. Your doctor will monitor your kidney function and drug levels with blood tests during treatment. Tell your doctor right away if you notice ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, or decreased urination. Avoid this medication if you are pregnant unless absolutely necessary, as it may harm the baby.
typical_dosing: When given as an injection or IV, dosing is carefully calculated based on your weight and kidney function, usually once every 8 to 24 hours as determined by your doctor. For eye infections, one to two drops are typically placed in the affected eye every 4 to 8 hours. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions.
